tasks.title: Add AppState notify/router helper
tasks.description:
Creare un choke point unico per emissione notifiche, preferibilmente `AppState::notify`, evitando match manuali nei producer.

---
**Completion summary:**
SUPERSEDED by the T493 raise-path redesign — the single choke point exists, it is just not `AppState::notify`. Every notification goes through `Notification::…send()` (the public door) → the host-installed sink → `AppEvent::RaiseNotification` → `notification::raise(state, draft)` (heca/src/notification.rs), which is the ONE place `Instant::now()` is read and the only non-test caller of `NotificationRuntime::push`. tasks.title: Implement none notification mode
tasks.description:
Quando `notification_system = "none"`, sopprimere i producer non critici del piano senza sopprimere stderr/debug logs.

---
**Completion summary:**
SHIPPED (commit bfabbb7 / this session): `[settings.notification_system] mode = "none"` suppresses every notification. tasks.title: Define v1 behavior for system notification mode
tasks.description:
DECIDED (Antonio, 2026-08-28): the OS-notification backend is a ROUTING SINK behind Notification::send(), NOT a component.

THE MODEL:
- Notification::send() stays the only door. A producer never knows or cares where a notification surfaces — it types Notification::info("…").send() and nothing else.
- Where it surfaces is a host routing decision, invisible to the caller, driven by [settings.notification_system] mode:
  - "app"    → the in-app ToastStack (today's path via notification::raise → NotificationRuntime::push).
  - "system" → the OS backend (P063): macOS Notification Center, Linux libnotify, Windows toast. An OS notification has no bounds, no parent, no input — it is NOT a widget in heca's tree, which is exactly why it is a sink and not a component. Antonio's "place it anywhere and it handles itself" rule does not apply to it.
  - "none"   → dropped (already implemented — suppressed()).
- The routing happens in ONE place: notification::raise (heca/src/notification.rs), which already reads the mode. Today: App and System both fall through to the in-app store. P063 adds the System arm — raise() hands the accepted draft to an installed OS sink instead of / in addition to the store.
- The OS sink is installed the same way the in-app sink is (install_notification_sink pattern) — host-installed once at startup, absent in a headless test.

v1 BEHAVIOUR FOR "system" BEFORE P063 LANDS (this task):
- mode = "system" falls back to the in-app toast (App behaviour) — already the case.
- ADD a one-time info notification on the first raise under mode="system" while no OS sink is installed: "OS notifications aren't available yet — showing in-app." dedup_key "notification.system.unavailable" so it appears once, not per notification. This is the only code T222 itself ships; the rest is the P063 phase.

CONSEQUENCES for P063: it builds the OS sink + its install point + the raise() System arm + per-OS spikes. It does NOT build a component, a widget, a layer, or anything in the tree. Update the P063 phase description to this model.

CONSEQUENCE for T381: declined_actions lives in this same [settings.notification_system] table and assumes this routing model — build T381 after this is recorded (done) or alongside P063.

tasks.title: A declined action says so — the producer for "nothing happened, and here is why"
tasks.description:
A declined action — one that runs, finds a precondition unmet, and returns without doing anything — currently vanishes. From a held key that is fine; from the command palette, where the user picked the entry out of a list, it reads as a broken command. Reported 2026-07-30: "Move Column Up" chosen in the palette did nothing (handle_move_column_up, heca/src/handlers.rs, returns early when current_ws == 0). Same silent early return: move_column_down, move_pane_*, copy_selection (no selection), open_link_at_caret (no link), scrollback paging at an edge, and a Provider::perform that returns Handled::No.

=== AGREED DESIGN (Antonio, 2026-08-28) — reusable, centralised, no hardcoding, no per-action flags ===

1. PICKED vs BOUND. Every invocation carries a small tag, orthogonal to InteractionSource and invisible to ActionPolicy:
   - Picked = user chose it from an explicit list: command palette, right-click menu, a clicked button, RPC.
   - Bound = user pressed a key mapped to it.
   Set in the few dispatch entry points, never per action. NOTE: the palette today dispatches as InteractionSource::Keyboard on purpose (heca/src/chrome/palette.rs:318-352) so policy judges it like the key — keep that; the tag rides alongside, it does not replace the source.

2. ONE DECLINE OUTCOME at the single chokepoint. dispatch_action / route_interaction (heca/src/app/interaction.rs) already computes Blocked / NotRunnable / MissingArgs and throws them away for every caller but RPC. Add the handler case: a handler that early-returns calls cx.decline("already at the top") through a sink on the context it already has, instead of a bare return. A handler that does NOT call it produces no notification — safe default, and migration is incremental (wire the handlers people complain about; the rest stay silent exactly as today). Do NOT special-case the two column actions; do NOT change ~100 handler signatures.

3. SURFACING is decided centrally from the tag + config, never by the action:
   [settings.notification_system]
   declined_actions = "picked"   # "picked" (default) | "all" | "off"
   - "picked": a decline from palette/menu/RPC/button raises a toast; a keybinding decline stays silent. Fixes the reported bug with zero navigation spam.
   - "all": keybinding declines also notify (deduped — a held key is one toast, not a stream). Nav actions (focus_*, scroll_*, scrollback) decline constantly, which is why this is opt-in, not default.
   - "off": never.
   Config: add a NotificationDeclined enum to NotificationSystemConfig (heca-config/src/settings.rs), serde snake_case, default Picked; document in config.default.toml + README; thread to wherever the chokepoint reads it.

4. THE TOAST is built centrally from the DeclineReason + the action's catalog label/icon (ActionCatalog), low severity, no modal, no sound: Notification::info(format!("{label} — {reason}")).dedup_key(format!("declined:{action}")).send(). The dedup_key collapses any leaked spray.

DEFERRED, separate: prevention — an optional can_perform(action) -> bool so the palette renders an entry disabled (DropdownItem already has an `enabled` flag) rather than letting it be chosen and decline. That is palette work (was F003/P085/T358), not this task. This task is about telling the user what happened.

BEHAVIOURS TO PRESERVE: a decline is NOT an error — low severity, no sound, no modal. Holding a key at a list edge must not spray (dedup + the Bound-is-silent default both cover it).

tasks.title: Add name-keyed `notify` action — the raise capability
tasks.description:
Raising a notification today is `state.notifications.push(NotificationDraft, now)` (heca/src/notification.rs, ported from origin/feature/notification-system@ceade1e) — a private Rust method on AppState's store. No plugin, RPC caller, or keybinding can reach it; only dismiss (NotificationDismissOne/All/Last, P059) is a real registered action. This closes that asymmetry.

What exists to build on: `register_dynamic(registry, catalog, meta, handler)` at heca/src/actions.rs:418, `unregister_dynamic` at heca/src/actions.rs:471 — the name-keyed action path documented in docs/widgets.md:4863 "Registering a custom (name-keyed) action". AGENTS.md:1554 "Adding New Actions", the paragraph after step 11: a name-keyed action skips steps 1-4/8 (no WmAction variant, no action_from_name/build_action/priority/ActionRegistry::ALL descriptor).

Register `notify` via register_dynamic — NOT a WmAction variant. A future WASM plugin can only ever dispatch by name, never add an enum variant, and "any plugin can raise a notification" is the point of this action.

Declared args (ArgSpec, pattern at docs/widgets.md:4897):
- title: Text, required
- body: Text, optional
- severity: Enum (info|success|warning|danger), optional, default info
- dedup_key: Text, optional

Handler builds a NotificationDraft from the args (NotificationDraft::new(title).body(..).severity(..).dedup_key(..)) and calls state.notifications.push(draft, Instant::now()).

No action-button argument in v1 — deliberate scope, not a widget limitation: ToastSpec/ToastAction already support several typed actions per card (T487, landed on heca-4b's side), but there is no ArgKind for a nested Intent, so an RPC caller or a keybinding has no typed way to say "and run this other action with these args" as one argument value. A Rust-internal caller that wants a button uses NotificationDraft::action(label, intent) directly with a real Intent it already holds — unaffected by this task.

ActionPolicy: Global (app-level, no layout impact, must keep working while a floating pane is up) — cross-check against T213.

Edge cases: wire RPC parser support in heca/src/rpc.rs same as any other action; a default keybinding is optional (raising a static notification via keybinding is an unusual use case — command palette + RPC are the primary doors).

---
**Completion summary:**
SHIPPED: register_notify_action(registry, catalog) in heca/src/notification.rs, called once from HecaApp::resumed() in main.rs (after providers::register_provider_actions). Registered via register_dynamic — no WmAction variant. Args: title(Text,required)/body(Text,optional)/severity(Enum,optional,default info)/dedup_key(Text,optional). Handler builds a NotificationDraft and calls state.notifications.push. ActionPolicy::Global. Added NotificationSeverity: EnumArg+FromStr (accepts info/success/warning/danger/error) for the severity arg's declared vocabulary. CORRECTION to this task's own "edge cases" text: no rpc.rs changes needed — confirmed the generic `action <name> key=val` RPC verb (heca/src/rpc.rs parse_rpc) already reaches any declared action generically, built-in or name-keyed, with zero per-action code. No default keybinding, by design (command palette + RPC are the doors). VERIFICATION: cargo check -p heca clean. NOT verified: never actually invoked yet (no running app). FILES: heca/src/notification.rs, heca/src/main.rs.

# F009 Notification System — near-complete; T381 + P063 remain

Created at: 2026-08-28
Updated at: 2026-08-28 (rev 3 — restored the cold-resume operational notes)
Reason: F009 is functionally complete and pushed. Full state for a context-free resume of T381
(declined-action producer) and P063 (OS backend), plus the new build guards and the planner /
testing / cross-session gotchas a fresh agent needs.

## 0. READ THIS FIRST — a fresh session starts in the MAIN checkout
- The work is on branch **`feat/notification-system-app`** in worktree
  `/Users/antonio/projects/myvim-code`. Tip `222daa0` (a rev-3 handoff commit bumps this). This
  handoff is a tracked `.planner/` file *on that branch* — if you are on `main` you will not see it
  until you `git checkout feat/notification-system-app` (or `cd` to the worktree). Once heca-57
  merges, it is on `feat/hint-anything-actionable` too.
- **`planner-handoff-show` returns an EMPTY payload — a real tool bug.** Use **`planner-handoff-list`**,
  which returns the full content. Do not proceed without reading it.
- **The planner drops large payloads SILENTLY** and still answers "✅ updated". Read back anything
  substantial you write (a phase/task description, a handoff). Long design content goes in a
  committed `docs/` file with the planner pointing at it.
- **Always use qualified refs `P0xx(F0xx)/Txxx`** — bare `T###` collide with heca-57's planner
  (two `.planner/` dirs merged via git, both allocating small sequential numbers).
- **One task in-progress at a time** across the whole planner (`ACTIVE_TASK_CONFLICT` otherwise).
  Every `planner-task-start` / `-switch` needs a fresh `full=true` read of that exact task + its
  phase + `F009` *immediately* before — a read one tool-call stale is rejected.
- **Do NOT pull heca-57's branch.** This tree is based on `ac0e71b`; nothing added here is a
  registry call, so it stays green through heca-57's merge. Pulling mid-stream only churns.

## 0b. Cross-session coordination
`heca-57` runs in `/Users/antonio/projects/heca` on `heca-grid-ui/` / `heca-view-realize/` /
`heca-renderer/` (the widget layer + `ToastStack`, `ToastSpec`, `ToastAction`, `LayerRegistry`).
This session owns **`heca/` + `heca-config/` + the default `.toml` files only**. Never edit
anything under `heca-grid-ui/`, `heca-view-realize/`, `heca-renderer/` — if a widget change seems
needed, stop and `SendMessage` heca-57 (address `uds:/tmp/cc-socks/33946.sock`).
heca-57 **merges `feat/notification-system-app` into its branch ONLY when this session sends an
explicit "ready to merge" message with the tip SHA** — a push alone is not the signal (Antonio's
instruction, 2026-08-28). heca-57's reporting protocol, match it: run a centralization grep (any
pattern written more than once) before reporting progress and state the count; report in
user-visible behaviour, never internal identifiers; say plainly what still needs Antonio to drive
vs what only compiled / passed tests.

## 0c. How to manually test a notification (there is NO RPC transport)
`heca/src/rpc.rs` parsing is complete, but nothing outside the process can reach it —
`HecaApp::execute_rpc_command` is `#[expect(dead_code)]` with zero callers, no socket/listener
anywhere. **Do not tell Antonio "test it via RPC".** The only way to see a toast today: insert a
temporary `crate::notification::Notification::info("Test").body("hello").send();` right after
`crate::chrome::mount_notification_stack(&mut state);` in `heca/src/app/startup.rs`, run
`cargo run -p heca`, remove the line after. The `notify` name-keyed action exists (args
`title` required, `body` / `severity` / `dedup_key` optional; no action-button arg in v1 — a scope
choice, there is no `ArgKind` for a nested `Intent`) but is only reachable from a keybinding, since
RPC has no transport. Whether `[[keys.component]]` config bindings support inline args was never
verified — do not assume.

## ⛔ NEW BUILD GUARDS — did not exist when this session started
- **`heca/tests/surface_drift.rs`** fails the build when a surface is **registered** instead of
  placed in the tree — any `state.layers.insert` / `add_named` / `add_view` **outside the

  Same shape as `heca-grid-ui/tests/prop_drift.rs`.
- Four grandfathered files in `KNOWN_REGISTRY_SURFACES`: `chrome/palette.rs`,
  `chrome/notification_layer.rs`, `chrome/overlay.rs`, `chrome/expose/mod.rs`. A second test flags
  a stale entry. **A NEW surface must be a tree node, never a registry call.**
- **`AGENTS.md § 0d`** = Antonio's FIRST RULE: a component owns its own input — put it anywhere and
  the host teaches it nothing. Test: `Overlay::new().child(Pane::new("editor").child(Terminal::new("shell")))`.
- **`docs/surface-compositor.md § 0`** is now the whole surfaces-and-input picture.
  **`docs/input-architecture.md` is a redirect stub — do NOT add content to it.**
- **`P097` moved to `F003`**; its terminal-viewport task canceled for `P094(F011)/T449`.
- heca-57 shipped the **scene seam** (`fd4a0b2`, `4d8d1bd`) — a widget can request host-only work
  (place rasterised content, blur behind it). Nothing emits it yet. Frost + terminal switch next,
  P094, heca-57's crates. Not yours.

## Current focus
Nothing in progress. F009 is functionally complete. Remaining, both deliberately not built:
`P055(F009)/T381` (declined-action producer — full design in the task) and phase `P063` (OS
backend — deferred, routing-sink architecture in the phase description). `P055/T223` also deferred.

## What was being done
Finishing F009: P055 (producers), P057 (tests + README), earlier P061/P062. Commits on
`feat/notification-system-app`, oldest → newest: `bfabbb7` (raise door + pane-creation producer +
notification_system config) · `0227019` (T207 cancel) · `6d0765b` (config-reload producer / P062) ·
`b53f9ff` (Retry dismisses the failure toast) · `3e37585` (pane-exit + spawn-fail producers +
tests + README / P055+P057) · `bb914b9` (OS-backend = routing-sink decision) · `8517257`
(mode="system" one-time fallback notice / T222) · `d4b6d6b`/`222daa0` (this handoff).

### The raise architecture (P061/T493 — done)
`notification::raise(state, draft)` in `heca/src/notification.rs` = the ONE place `Instant::now()`
is read for a raised notification and the only non-test caller of `NotificationRuntime::push`. Both
doors converge on it: `Notification::…send()` (public builder → thread-local sink installed in
`heca/src/app/startup.rs` → `AppEvent::RaiseNotification` → handled in `heca/src/main.rs`) and the
name-keyed `notify` action. `NotificationStore::push` + `NotificationRuntime::push` are
`pub(crate)`; `Notification` is the only public raise surface; `Notification::sticky()` opts out of
auto-dismiss. `NotificationActionRelay` (a toast button) is classified `Global` in `action_policy`
and re-fires the stored `Intent` through the router (`handle_notification_action_relay` in
`heca/src/handlers.rs`), never a direct handler.

### Config — `[settings.notification_system]` (P061/T186/T187/T191 + T503 — done)
`heca-config/src/settings.rs`: `NotificationSystemConfig { mode: NotificationSystem, auto_dismiss_ms: u64 }`.
`mode = "app" | "system" | "none"` (default `App`): `none` → `raise()` early-returns via
`suppressed()`; `system` → in-app fallback + one-time notice (`system_fallback_notice()`, T222).
`auto_dismiss_ms` (default 4000) applied at the runtime boundary in `push()` via
`NotificationLifecycle::with_auto_duration`. `set_auto_dismiss` / `set_mode` re-applied on
`prefix+Shift+r` (`heca/src/main.rs`). Documented in `config.default.toml` + `README.md`
("### Notifications"). **T503:** `default_lifetime_for_severity` DELETED — severity does not change
lifetime, everything auto-dismisses, `.sticky()` opts out. **Reversible** (re-add the mapping in
the draft severity setters) if Antonio wants errors sticky by default.

### Producers (P055)
- **T491** `notify` action — done pre-session.
- **T221** pane-exited — `heca/src/app/process_monitor.rs::notify_pane_exited(pane, code)`: a pane
  whose process exits *while it stays open* → Info (exit 0) / Warning + "exit code N",
  `dedup_key "pane.exited:<id>"`, Focus action. Auto-closing panes → nothing.
- **T225** spawn-failed — `create_command_backend_for_state` / `_with_options`
  (`heca/src/app/backend_factory.rs`) now return `Result<Box<dyn PaneBackend>, String>` (command
  path only; shell/terminal keeps its `FakeBackend` fallback). `handle_spawn_command` builds the
  backend before layout; `Err` → sticky danger, no empty pane.
- **T219** superseded, **T220** done, **T224** done (park), **T222** done.
- Pane-creation: `announce_pane_created(pane_id)` in `heca/src/handlers.rs`, all 5 user-initiated
  creation handlers; `Notification::info("Pane {id} created")` + Focus action. Id not name (fresh
  pane has none) — Antonio accepted this.

### Config-reload producer (P062 — done)
`heca/src/main.rs`: `reload_config()` → `Result<(), ConfigError>`; `notify_reload_outcome()`
(extracted, tested): success → auto-dismiss "Configuration reloaded"; failure → **sticky** "Config
reload failed" + parse-error body + **Retry** (`dismiss_after: true`, fires the existing
`reload_config` action). Shared `dedup_key "config-reload"`. stderr lines kept.

### Tests + docs (P057 — done, 8/8)
The 67-test `notification.rs` suite covers store lifecycle / dedup / model conversion / config
parsing. Added this session: send-door, sticky, dedup-replace, relay action-resolution,
pane-exited producer, reload-outcome smoke, system-fallback. README "### Notifications" section.
`notification-system-plane.md` is a superseded pre-planner analysis — leave it (heca-57 maintains).

## How to resume
1. `cd /Users/antonio/projects/myvim-code` (or checkout `feat/notification-system-app`). Do not
   pull heca-57's branch.
2. `./scripts/lint-changed.sh test` then `./scripts/lint-changed.sh` — **never `--workspace`**
   (20+ min). Both exit 0 today; only 2 `heca-grid-ui` warnings (heca-57's).
3. **T381**: `planner-task-show P055(F009)/T381 full=true` — it carries the complete agreed design:
   a **picked-vs-bound** invocation tag, orthogonal to `InteractionSource`, invisible to
   `ActionPolicy` (Picked = palette / menu / clicked button / RPC; Bound = a keybinding). One
   decline outcome at the `dispatch_action` / `route_interaction` chokepoint
   (`heca/src/app/interaction.rs` — it already computes `Blocked` / `NotRunnable` / `MissingArgs`
   and discards them for non-RPC callers). Handlers report a precondition decline via a
   `cx.decline("…")` sink instead of a bare early `return` — silent by default, so migration is
   incremental (wire the handlers people complain about, e.g. `handle_move_column_up` at ws 0).
   Central toast builder from the reason + `ActionCatalog` label, `dedup_key "declined:<action>"`.
   Config: `[settings.notification_system] declined_actions = "picked" | "all" | "off"` default
   `"picked"` (`NotificationDeclined` enum, `heca-config/src/settings.rs`). The palette dispatches
   as `InteractionSource::Keyboard` on purpose (`heca/src/chrome/palette.rs:318-352`) — the tag
   rides alongside, does not replace the source. Deferred/separate: `can_perform(action)->bool` →
   grey palette entries (`DropdownItem` already has an `enabled` flag).
4. **P063**: `planner-phase-show P063 full=true` — full routing-sink model. Build
   `SystemNotificationBackend` trait + install point (same `install_notification_sink` pattern) +
   the `System` arm in `notification::raise` + per-OS spikes (notify-rust: libnotify/D-Bus, macOS
   UNUserNotificationCenter, Windows toast) + failure-fallback to in-app + action-button round-trip
   through the same relay. **No component / widget / layer / tree node** — a sink is not a registry
   call, so `surface_drift.rs` is fine with it.

## Files touched
`heca/src/notification.rs`, `heca/src/main.rs`, `heca/src/handlers.rs`,
`heca/src/app/process_monitor.rs`, `heca/src/app/backend_factory.rs`, `heca/src/app/startup.rs`,

- **T223** deferred — `Provider::perform` (`heca/src/providers/mod.rs`) returns `Handled` only

- **P063** deferred — its own phase.

## ⛔ Do NOT touch
- `heca/src/chrome/notification_layer.rs` — collides with heca-57's `P097(F003)` **and** is a
  grandfathered `surface_drift.rs` file. Message heca-57 if a change seems needed.
- The six oversized-file splits in P082 (`handlers.rs`, `actions.rs`, `app/interaction.rs`,

- Any `P097(F003)` task — heca-57's. `docs/input-architecture.md` (redirect stub).
- `cargo fmt` in this repo (rustfmt 1.9 churns unrelated files — hand-format).

## Next steps
1. `P055(F009)/T381` — declined-action producer (design captured; fresh-session build).
2. `P063` — OS backend (deferred; routing-sink model recorded).
3. `P055(F009)/T223` — provider/plugin error producer (deferred).
4. **Antonio drives every visual check** — none of F009 driven end to end. Two toast-card defects
   on heca-57's side: `P096(F003)/T504` (same-id toast card never re-renders — my Retry
   `dismiss_after` works around it) and `T505` (bodyless toast card: title and × on different lines).

## Recent decisions
- **OS backend is a routing sink behind `Notification::send()`, not a component** (Antonio
  2026-08-28) — an OS notification has no bounds/parent/input, so it is not a widget in heca's
  tree; `mode` routes the accepted draft in `notification::raise`, one place. On T222 + P063.
- **Severity is tone, not importance** — no per-severity lifetime, no priority field (T503). Every
  notification auto-dismisses; `.sticky()` opts out. Reversible.
- **`Notification::send()` is the only public raise door**; both `push` methods `pub(crate)`; one
  `Instant::now()` site (`raise`) — so the caller never passes a clock and never names the store's
  verb.
- **Declined-action pattern (T381)** — the source (picked vs bound), not the action, decides
  whether a decline surfaces; nothing hardcoded per action. Grey-out prevention deferred.
- **T207 canceled** — its pointer-passthrough half was never validation, it is the P097
  input-architecture phase; acceptance criteria folded into `P097(F003)/T500`.
- **Antonio's FIRST RULE (`AGENTS.md § 0d`)** — a component owns its own input; put it anywhere,
  the host teaches it nothing. Governs every widget/component going forward.
- No timestamp/delay argument on `Notification` — `.now()` / `.at()` both proposed and rejected;
  absent means deliver now, host stamps the clock (carried from the T493 redesign).
